name: Edmonton
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Edmonton: Alberta public procurement, energy contractors, Law Courts records and asset research for counsel.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Edmonton, scoped from Nashville: research on contractors and suppliers to Alberta's public sector and energy industry, corporate and court records filed in the Law Courts, and factual support for counsel in recovery, procurement and employment matters.
intro: Edmonton is Alberta's capital and the province's second-largest city. City of Edmonton figures put the population at about 1.20 million on 1 July 2024 and about 1.24 million in 2025, with the census metropolitan area at about 1.64 million in 2024 after growth of more than five percent in a single year, driven by record net migration. The 2025 Edmonton Business Census counted almost 30,000 businesses employing about 575,000 people, with services accounting for 88 percent of establishments. Retail, health care, construction and professional services are major employers, alongside the provincial government, post-secondary institutions and the industrial and energy service companies that support northern Alberta's resource economy.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Edmonton for reasons that differ from Calgary's head-office profile. As the seat of the provincial government, the city concentrates public procurement, grant funding and regulatory decision-making, which produces integrity questions about contractors, consultants and lobbyists. Its role as a supply, fabrication and logistics base for oil sands and industrial projects creates exposure to inflated invoicing, kickbacks and contractor insolvencies. A fast-growing population and construction sector bring real estate, lending and builder disputes. Employers investigating misconduct, insurers testing claims and creditors pursuing judgment debtors all need well-sourced information about companies and individuals in Alberta.

matters.title: Public sector procurement integrity
matters.text: Research supporting reviews of contracts and grants awarded by public bodies in the capital, including background on vendors, consultants and their principals, related companies, and connections between suppliers and decision-makers that may indicate undisclosed conflicts, for internal audit, counsel or compliance teams.

matters.title: Industrial contractor and supplier fraud
matters.text: Support to internal investigations into kickbacks, duplicate or inflated invoicing and phantom vendors on fabrication, maintenance and construction work serving northern Alberta energy and industrial projects, through lawful research into suppliers, their owners and links to employees.

matters.title: Judgment enforcement and asset research
matters.text: Assembling public-record information for creditors and counsel on debtors and their principals in the Edmonton region, including corporate interests, registered security, land holdings disclosed in provincial registers and transfers to related parties, before enforcement steps are taken through the courts.

matters.title: Construction and real estate disputes
matters.text: Background research on builders, developers and trades in a rapidly growing metropolitan area, covering prior insolvencies, litigation, licensing references and the companies behind project vehicles, to help lenders, purchasers and counsel assess counterparties or prepare for litigation.

matters.title: Workplace misconduct and claims
matters.text: Factual research supporting employers and insurers in Edmonton on suspected conflicts of interest, outside business activity or questionable claims, using public records and open sources, with any interviews or surveillance carried out only by appropriately licensed Alberta investigators.

local_context.title: Law Courts building
local_context.text: Edmonton's Law Courts at 1A Sir Winston Churchill Square, opened in 1973, house the Provincial Court of Alberta, the Court of King's Bench of Alberta and the Court of Appeal of Alberta. The Court of King's Bench is the province's superior trial court and hears major civil, commercial and insolvency matters. The Court of Appeal sits only in Edmonton and Calgary, with roughly equal numbers of justices stationed in each city.

local_context.title: Alberta investigator licensing
local_context.text: Alberta licenses private and in-house investigators under the Security Services and Investigators Act, administered by the provincial government from Edmonton. Interviews, surveillance and other field enquiries in Alberta therefore need licensed personnel. TDSC does not hold an Alberta licence and coordinates with appropriately licensed Alberta professionals where a matter requires local field work. Desk research on public records can still be performed from Nashville, and the client's Canadian counsel advises on admissibility and privacy.

local_context.title: Provincial registries and privacy
local_context.text: Alberta's corporate registry, land titles and personal property registry are provincial systems, generally accessed through authorised registry agents, while federally incorporated companies are searched through Corporations Canada. Private-sector personal information, including employee information, is governed for most purposes by Alberta's Personal Information Protection Act. Each register answers a different question and none shows bank balances. Searches are combined with court filings and open sources.

local_context.title: Seat of provincial government
local_context.text: As the capital, Edmonton is where provincial ministries, agencies and the Legislature make procurement, funding and regulatory decisions. Public records such as published contract disclosures, legislative materials and agency decisions can help establish who was paid and on what basis. Research in this area is limited to lawfully available records and open sources and does not involve access to restricted government systems.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Edmonton, TDSC first establishes whether the question is about a public-sector relationship, an industrial supply chain, a debtor or an individual, because each points to different Alberta and federal records. Research is conducted from Nashville using corporate and land registry results obtained through proper channels, Court of King's Bench and Court of Appeal filings and decisions, published government contract information and open sources. Alberta licenses investigators, so any interviews, surveillance or field enquiries are carried out by appropriately licensed Alberta professionals coordinated by TDSC with the client's Canadian counsel. Personal information is handled consistently with Alberta's Personal Information Protection Act, and findings are reported with their sources and stated limits.

faqs.q: Can you research a contractor to the Alberta government?
faqs.a: Yes. We review the contractor's corporate history, directors and related companies, litigation in Alberta courts, published contract and grant information, media coverage and any regulatory decisions. Where a conflict of interest is suspected we look for public links between the contractor and decision-makers. Conclusions about whether rules were breached remain with the client's counsel and auditors.

faqs.q: Which courts in Edmonton handle commercial disputes?
faqs.a: Significant commercial, insolvency and civil matters are heard by the Court of King's Bench of Alberta, which sits in the Law Courts in downtown Edmonton. Appeals go to the Court of Appeal of Alberta, which also sits in the same building. The Provincial Court handles smaller civil claims. We research filings and published decisions across these courts.

faqs.q: How do you help with suspected supplier kickbacks on an industrial project?
faqs.a: Forensic accountants test the transactions. We support counsel by researching suspect vendors, their owners and addresses, overlaps with employees' families or associates, and other companies sharing directors. The output is a sourced map of relationships that helps counsel decide on interviews, audit steps or civil recovery.

faqs.q: Can TDSC conduct surveillance in Edmonton?
faqs.a: TDSC does not hold an Alberta investigator licence and does not conduct surveillance itself. Where surveillance is lawful and proportionate for the matter, it is carried out by appropriately licensed Alberta investigators whom TDSC coordinates, with the client's counsel advising on privacy and admissibility. Many matters are resolved through public-record research alone.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Edmonton?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in Edmonton or elsewhere in Canada. Engagements touching the city are scoped and managed from Nashville, with licensed Alberta investigators and the client's Canadian counsel engaged where field work or legal advice is needed.
